pitch: Reciprocity, commitment, social proof, liking, authority, scarcity: the mechanisms that make us say yes, and how to defend yourself.
br: bystanders · no one acts · single out
quiz: According to Cialdini, what do most persuasion techniques rest on?
A small number of universal psychological principles
They are mental shortcuts that can be exploited.
What does the turquoise jewelry story illustrate?
The price doubled by mistake made the jewelry sell.
Ask for little, then a lot
Ask for a lot, then a more moderate request perceived as a concession
A concession calls for a concession.
What is the “foot in the door”?
Getting a small commitment before a bigger request
The first yes changes self-image and pushes you to stay consistent.
Why do many bystanders intervene less?
Diffusion of responsibility and pluralistic ignorance
Hence the advice: single out a specific person.
Which experiment illustrates the authority principle?
A majority obeyed a researcher to the very end.
What did the cookie experiment show?
Especially when the scarcity is new and linked to others' demand.
Which principle was added in the 2021 edition?
We say yes to those we see as “one of us.”
